title: Process Simulation & Optimization for Thin-Ply Composites
description: This Phase III STTR project develops process simulation tools and best practices for thin-ply  thermoset and thermoplastics composites to reduce distortion

title: Gas Detection System for Cure Process Management of Polyimide Composites
description: This Direct to Phase II SBIR seeks to improve processing capabilities and yield of polyimide-based carbon fiber reinforced polymers (CFRPs) through development of an integrated hardware tool that allows detection, identification, and quantification of species removed from the system in near real time.

title: Heat Blanket Design and Thermal Compliance
description: This project developed a workflow-based tool that interrogates the effect of local changes to boundary conditions such as heat transfer coefficient (HTC) on the thermal profile. To accomplish this, heating techniques and local HTCs were characterized in parallel to supporting software features

title: Bagging Variability and Thickness Prediction
description: Characterization & modeling of consumables impact on part quality with a focus on porosity and exploration of parametric simulation

title: Thermal Modeling Base High-Temperature Polymer Matrix Composite (PMC) Structural Repair
description: Repair processes involve uniform heating of a local area, which can be difficult, as location variations and substructure can contribute to a non-uniform heat profile and cause the repair to fall outside of thermal specifications. Convergent US developed a workflow and toolset that allow the user to model different repair strategies and their thermal outcomes, thereby reducing the need for costly iterative thermal surveys and/or trial-and-error testing.

title: Process Simulation & Optimization for Advanced Tailorable Composites
description: This Phase I SBIR project developed a process simulation workflow for process optimization and part quality prediction of composite parts to enable tailored manufacturing processes. The workflow mapped physics-based process simulation of local outcomes and defects with the simulation of the effects of the outcomes on part quality.

title: Innovative Methods for Thermoplastic Composites on ATL/AFP
description: AFP methods offer unique manufacturing benefits but are subject to defects during deposition, including wrinkles due to tack or weld quality issues. Deposition rates are slowed to improve part quality, leading to a longer processing time that can be optimized through simulation. The goal of the AF Phase II work was to improve AFP thermoplastic deposition rates by 30% or more with the same or better part quality (as measured by distortion) using process simulation and optimization.

title: AFP Defect Prediction for NASA's Advanced Composites Project
description: The AFP process tools developed under this contract focus on the prediction of defects during deposition in AFP based on the competing phenomena of tack and internal stress development. This project developed capabilities for characterization and explicit modeling of AFP-related defects (puckers, wrinkles, etc.).

title: Coupled Cure Infusion Simulation
description: This Phase I effort demonstrated a methodology for linking an infusion code with a cure and residual stress/deformation model by strategically evaluating separate codes for each phenomenon and providing an implementation method for a coupled solution.
